title: Aventine Retail - First-week ramp and platform handshake

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-05 14:00 UTC | Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Carlos (Redwood CSM); Tom, Priya, Evan, Leah, Sam (Aventine)
---
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick roll call — we good?
[00:05] Tom: Yep, Tom here. Good to go.
[00:09] Priya: Priya on my end. Thanks.
[00:12] Jordan: Awesome. High-level, today is a handshake: first-week ramp, access windows, security constraints, and how we measure pilot success. Maya will cover the infra checklist. Carlos will cover the logistics.
[00:24] Maya: Hi all. I'll run through what we typically ask for a private pilot — VPC peering, NAT/egress rules, SSO service account, and sample payloads. Note some of our notes are auto-generated so there may be typos — e.g., "KV cache" got logged as "K V cash" in one doc.
[00:40] Priya: Good call. On workload, we have two main flows: checkout assistant (short prompts, high qps) and product QA summarizer (longer context, lower qps). We'll share typical token distributions.
[00:55] Maya: Perfect. For throughput reasoning, that helps with batching and quantization recommendations. Quick note — if you want Redwood Dedicated, we can reserve capacity; if you go Hosted first you get faster setup but less network isolation.
[01:12] Leah: On security, our baseline is SOC2-like controls, SAML SSO, and KMS for key management. We need audit logs that show request-level metadata for 90 days. Can you confirm?
[01:26] Jordan: Yes — we can provide audit events and our console retains token-costing per-request. For KMS, we integrate with customers' KM S (sometimes shows as K M S in the export) — AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or HSM. There may be slight mismatches in the field names in the auto-exports.
[01:44] Sam: Are there data residency controls? We need the inference to stay in our eu-west-1 account for now.
[01:52] Jordan: Absolutely. For Private deployment we can keep everything inside your VPC in eu-west-1. For Hosted, you can pin region but the data path may cross. We should flag that if data residency is hard requirement, Private is the right route.
[02:10] Tom: We want to start with a two-week pilot — validate latency and cost, then decide on Dedicated vs Private. Is that a reasonable split?
[02:17] Carlos: Totally reasonable. Our recommended plan: week 0 (this week) — access and sandbox; week 1 — runbench and monitoring; week 2 — iterate prompts and tuning, then a go/no-go.
[02:31] Priya: For the runbench, can you simulate peak QPS? We have spike windows during promotions.
[02:36] Maya: We can run load tests that mimic your qps curve. We'll need your traffic patterns and API keys for sandbox. Also please indicate whether you use KV-cache heavy workloads; that's helpful for prefix caching suggestions.
[02:52] Evan: On that — our caching is in-house and we pass session tokens. I worried about cold-starts and latency tail.
[03:00] Maya: We'll instrument tail latency and suggest batching windows. Often a 10-30ms addition is from network in VPC peering; compute tails depend on GPU type and sequence length.
[03:14] Leah: About SSO: we use Okta and want users to map to RBAC roles in Redwood Console. How granular can the roles be?
[03:23] Jordan: You can map Okta groups to Console roles. We support admin, devops, observer, and custom lanes. We'll send the SAML metadata and attribute mapping doc.
[03:35] Priya: Anything about encryption at rest for cached artifacts? We want KV cache encrypted.
[03:41] Maya: Cache objects can be encrypted with your KMS if on Private. On Hosted, cache at rest is encrypted with platform keys but can opt-in to bring-your-own-key for dedicated. I'll get exact details.
[03:55] Tom: Timeline question: if we sign off on the pilot by Friday, how quickly can you spin a pilot in our VPC?
[04:03] Carlos: Our typical window is 48-72 hours once we get the peering window and service account. There can be delays if firewall rules are strict.
[04:12] Sam: Let's talk about observability — we need per-route latency, token breakdown by caller, and error rate alerts.
[04:20] Maya: Console provides per-route dashboards, token breakdown, and trace links. For alerts we can hook into your PagerDuty or Webhooks. We'll include the doc with sample queries.
[04:32] Priya: On cost — we need a ballpark per-100k-token cost for the pilot and for a projected monthly QPS.
[04:38] Jordan: We'll send a pricing appendix in an email. Cost depends on model choice and quantization. For example, a 7B quantized variant could be X cents per 1k tokens vs a full 70B model is more. (note: numbers in call not provided intentionally; we'll follow up).
[04:55] Evan: Anything special for legal — e.g., data retention, PII handling?
[05:00] Jordan: For PII we recommend on-the-fly redaction in the app layer and masking. We can also set shorter audit retention if needed. Legal review can be scheduled with our legal ops.
[05:10] Leah: We need an auditable SLA for latency percentiles — can that be scoped into the pilot?
[05:16] Carlos: We can commit to measuring p50/p95 in the dashboard and agree on a target for the pilot. SLA contracts are typically part of Dedicated or Private contracts. For pilot we provide targets and measurement.
[05:30] Tom: Great. Let's run through immediate ownership: who sends the peering window, who sets up SSO, who runs runbench?
[05:36] Priya: We'll own sending traffic profiles and the SSO admin. Leah will own the KMS policy confirmation. Sam will coordinate infra times.
[05:44] Jordan: Redwood will send the pilot timeline and infra checklist (Jordan), Maya will provide the ops checklist and runbench plan, Carlos will schedule calendar and invite.
[05:56] Priya: Quick Q about model variants — do you have pre-verified quantized models that preserve quality?
[06:04] Maya: Yes, we maintain a model catalog with verified performance profiles. For certain workloads we recommend a specific quant profile; we'll include eval examples. Note: sometimes the auto-doc calls them "Redwood verified" or "Rwood verify" — ignore spelling diffs.
[06:21] Tom: Any blockers you foresee?
[06:24] Maya: Only blockers I can see are delayed peering windows or SSO config time. Also if you need regional-only hosting and we haven't set up a Private deployment in that region yet, that could add lead time.
[06:38] Priya: We'll target getting the peering window by Friday EOD.
[06:43] Jordan: OK. Proposed concrete dates: Maya to drop infra checklist by Wed 2026-05-06; Jordan to send pilot timeline + pricing by Thu 2026-05-07; runbench scheduled Tue 2026-05-12. Does that work?
[06:58] Tom: Works for us.
[07:00] Evan: Slight aside — do you support function/tool calling to our internal vector DB?
[07:06] Maya: We support tool calling patterns and embeddings pipelines. For vectors we integrate with endpoints or send embedding batches. We'll sync with your infra about where the vector DB lives.
[07:18] Leah: Also need to ensure audit logs include user email and internal request id.
[07:23] Jordan: We'll include request_id and user attributes in the export.
[07:28] Priya: If we identify quality regressions during the pilot, how do rollbacks work?
[07:33] Carlos: We support pinning model versions, automatic fallback policies, and can route traffic back to a stable model. We'll include the rollback doc.
[07:44] Tom: Anything else?
[07:45] Maya: One last ops note — please include a sample of worst-case long-context prompt, even if rare; it helps with kernel selection and memory planning.
[07:56] Priya: Will do.
[08:00] Jordan: Recap: we have owners and dates. I'll recap in the follow-up email and attach the runner checklist and SAML mapping doc.
[08:10] Tom: Thanks everyone. Looking forward.
[08:15] Jordan: Thanks — talk soon.
---
Meeting end.
Recap (auto): Send pilot timeline, infra checklist, runbench schedule. Agreed two-week pilot focused on latency and cost, with week-1 benchmarks and week-2 tuning.
Notes about transcription: minor mis-hearings (KMS -> K M S, KV cache -> K V cash), some speaker labels genericized.
